title: Merge Intervals
statement:
Merge every group of overlapping intervals in a list into one interval, and print the intervals that are left.

The first line is the number of intervals `n`, at least 1. Each of the next `n` lines is one interval as `start end`, two whole numbers where `start` is at most `end`. The intervals can come in any order. Two intervals overlap when they share at least one point, so intervals that only touch, like `1 2` and `2 3`, merge into `1 3`. Print the merged intervals from the earliest start to the latest, one per line as `start end`.

Input:

```text
4
1 3
2 6
8 10
15 18
```

Expected output:

```text
1 6
8 10
15 18
```
hints: Sort the intervals by start first. Then every interval that overlaps the one you are building comes right after it.
Keep a list of merged intervals. When the next interval starts at or before the end of the last merged one, stretch that end. Otherwise it starts a new merged interval.
When you stretch, keep the larger of the two ends, since one interval can sit entirely inside another.
